'''Tom Ilmanen''' (1961–2025<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ch/|title = News|access-date=January 9, 2026|publisher=Swiss Mathematical Society}}</ref>) was an American [[mathematician]] specializing in [[differential geometry]] and the [[calculus of variations]]. He was a professor at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="ETHprofile">{{cite web | title=Prof. Dr. Tom Ilmanen| website=ETH Zurich - Department of Mathematics | date=2020-05-11 | url=https://math.ethz.ch/research/geometric-analysis-pde/tom-ilmanen.html | access-date=2025-03-31}}</ref> He obtained his PhD in 1991 at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] with [[Lawrence Craig Evans]] as supervisor.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=31671}}</ref> Ilmanen and [[Gerhard Huisken]] used [[inverse mean curvature flow]] to prove<ref name="PenroseInequality">{{cite journal | last1=Huisken | first1=Gerhard | last2=Ilmanen | first2=Tom | title=The Inverse Mean Curvature Flow and the Riemannian Penrose Inequality | journal=Journal of Differential Geometry | volume=59 | issue=3 | date=2001-11-01 | issn=0022-040X | doi=10.4310/jdg/1090349447 | doi-access=free | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/journal-of-differential-geometry/volume-59/issue-3/The-Inverse-Mean-Curvature-Flow-and-the-Riemannian-Penrose-Inequality/10.4310/jdg/1090349447.pdf | access-date=2025-03-31 | pages=353–437}}</ref> the [[Riemannian Penrose inequality|Riemannian Penrose conjecture]], which is the fifteenth problem in [[Shing-Tung Yau|Yau]]'s list of open problems,<ref>{{cite book | last1=Greene | first1=Robert Everist |author-link=Robert Everist Greene | last2=Yau | first2=Shing-Tung | title=Differential Geometry: Partial Differential Equations on Manifolds | series=Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics | date=1993 | volume=54.1 | doi=10.1090/pspum/054.1 | isbn=978-0-8218-1494-9 }}</ref> and was resolved at the same time in greater generality by [[Hubert Bray]] using alternative methods.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Mars | first1=Marc | title=Present status of the Penrose inequality | journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity | date=2009 | volume=26 | issue=19 | doi=10.1088/0264-9381/26/19/193001 | arxiv=0906.5566 }}</ref>

In their 2001 paper,<ref name="PenroseInequality"/> Huisken and Ilmanen made a conjecture on the mathematics of [[general relativity]], about the [[curvature]] in spaces with very little [[mass]]: as the mass of the space shrinks to zero, the curvature of the space also shrinks to zero. This was proved in 2023 by Conghan Dong and [[Antoine Song]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-century-later-new-math-smooths-out-general-relativity-20231130/|title=A Century Later, New Math Smooths Out General Relativity|magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]]|date=30 November 2023|first=Steve|last=Nadis}}</ref><ref name="3-spaceStability">{{cite journal | last1=Dong | first1=Conghan | last2=Song | first2=Antoine | title=Stability of Euclidean 3-space for the positive mass theorem | journal=Inventiones Mathematicae | volume=239 | issue=1 | date=2025 | issn=0020-9910 | doi=10.1007/s00222-024-01302-z | pages=287–319| arxiv=2302.07414 | bibcode=2025InMat.239..287D }}</ref>

In an influential 1995 preprint,<ref>{{Cite arXiv | title = Singularities of mean curvature flow of surfaces|last1=Ilmanen | first1=Tom | date=1995 | class=math.DG | eprint=2601.21133}}</ref> Ilmanen made the following conjecture:
{{Blockquote
|text=For a smooth one-parameter family of closed embedded surfaces in Euclidean 3-space flowing by mean curvature, every tangent flow at the first singular time has multiplicity one. <ref name="ColdingMinicozzi">{{cite journal | last1=Colding | first1=Tobias | last2=Minicozzi | first2=William | title=Generic mean curvature flow I; generic singularities | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=175 | issue=2 | date=2012-03-01 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2012.175.2.7 | doi-access=free | pages=755–833 | url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p07-p.pdf | access-date=2025-04-01}}</ref>
}}
This has become known as the "multiplicity-one" conjecture. Richard Bamler and [[Bruce Kleiner]] proved the multiplicity-one conjecture in a 2023 preprint.<ref name="SmoothMelting">{{cite web | last=Nadis | first=Steve | title=A New Proof Smooths Out the Math of Melting | website=Quanta Magazine | date=2025-03-31 | url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-new-proof-smooths-out-the-math-of-melting-20250331/ | access-date=2025-03-31}}</ref><ref name="MultiplicityOne">{{cite arXiv | title=On the Multiplicity-One Conjecture for Mean Curvature Flows of Surfaces | last1=Bamler | first1=Richard | last2=Kleiner | first2=Bruce | date=2023 | class=math.DG | eprint=2312.02106 }}</ref>

Ilmanen received a [[Sloan Fellowship]] in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database|title=Fellows Database &#124; Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|website=sloan.org}}</ref>

He wrote the research monograph ''Elliptic Regularization and Partial Regularity for Motion by Mean Curvature''.<ref name="MAMS">{{cite book | last=Ilmanen | first=Tom | title=Elliptic Regularization and Partial Regularity for Motion by Mean Curvature | publisher=American Mathematical Soc. | publication-place=Providence, R.I | date=1994 | isbn=978-0-8218-2582-2 | page=}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*[[Gerhard Huisken|Huisken, Gerhard]], and Tom Ilmanen. "The inverse mean curvature flow and the Riemannian Penrose inequality." ''[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]'' 59.3 (2001): 353–437. DOI: 10.4310/jdg/1090349447
*Ilmanen, Tom. "Convergence of the Allen-Cahn equation to Brakke's motion by mean curvature." ''Journal of Differential Geometry'' 38.2 (1993): 417–461.
*Feldman, Mikhail, Tom Ilmanen, and Dan Knopf. "Rotationally symmetric shrinking and expanding gradient Kähler-Ricci solitons." ''Journal of Differential Geometry'' 65.2 (2003): 169–209.
